title: Drone debris kills two at a Saudi oilfield
credits: Photos: Wolfgang Hasselmann, Chris LeBoutillier, Keith Hardy / Unsplash · Map: Natural Earth
lines: Two workers have been killed in Saudi Arabia, after a drone was shot down near one of the kingdom's biggest oilfields.
On Wednesday, Saudi air defences intercepted a drone aimed at a processing plant at Aramco's Shaybah oilfield.
Shaybah lies deep in the Empty Quarter desert, near the border with the UAE, and produces about one million barrels of oil a day.
Falling debris set a contractor's vehicle on fire, outside the plant. A Filipino and a Nepali worker were killed.
Two more people were injured: one from Pakistan, and one from India.
Saudi Arabia's energy ministry says the oilfield's operations were not affected.
The Saudi-led coalition says it intercepted more drones the same day, including over the Madina region.
The Houthis in Yemen deny carrying out what they call deep operations inside Saudi territory.
The United States has now ordered non-emergency government staff and their families to leave Saudi Arabia.
On Thursday morning, Brent crude climbed above one hundred and ten dollars a barrel.
The Saudi-Houthi war, more than a decade old, reignited in July this year, and millions of South Asian workers in the Gulf are watching closely.
